    Sources indicate that mortgage rates are constantly changing, since a major part of how rates are set depends on reactions to newly introduced inflation reports, job numbers, Fed meetings, global news ... you name it. For example, even tiny changes in the bond market can shift mortgage pricing.

    Industry observers note that next week, the Nerds are waiting for the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index, due out Wednesday. It's the Federal Reserve's preferred measure of inflation, so investors will be watching closely. The Fed doesn't set mortgage rates, but lenders anticipate its decisions, so mortgage rates often move before the Fed acts. Stubbornly high inflation is a big reason why we’re seeing upward pressure on mortgage rates right now.

    If PCE indicates inflation comes in hotter than expected, mortgage rates could climb as markets anticipate further Fed rate hikes. (An increase to the federal funds rate is already widely expected at the Fed’s Dec. 8-9 meeting.) A cooler reading could ease some pressure on mortgage rates for now.

    I’m not getting my hopes up too high for meaningfully lower inflation, though. Last week's Producer Price Index showed wholesale inflation climbed 6.5% over the past year — its fastest pace in four years. Wholesale inflation measures the price businesses pay for things. When businesses’ costs go up, they could pass those along to consumers in the form of higher prices — keeping the flames of inflation alive.

    Whether Wednesday's PCE brings relief or another helping of bad inflation news, we'll know before the turkey hits the table on Thursday.

    Refinancing might make sense if today’s rates are at least 0.5 to 0.75 of a percentage point lower than your current rate (and if you plan to stay in your home long enough to break even on closing costs).

    With rates where they are right now, you may want to start considering a refi if your current rate is around 7.74% or higher.

    In a recent development, also consider your goals: Are you trying to lower your monthly payment, shorten your loan term or turn home equity into cash? For example, you might be more comfortable with paying a higher rate for a cash-out refinance than you would for a rate-and-term refinance, so long as the overall costs are lower than if you kept your original mortgage and added a HELOC or home equity loan.

    If you're looking for a lower rate, use NerdWallet's refinance calculator to estimate savings and understand how long it would take to break even on the costs of refinancing.

    There is no universal “right” time to start shopping — what matters is whether you can comfortably afford a mortgage now at today’s rates.

    If the answer is yes, don’t get too hung up on whether you could be missing out on lower rates later; you can refinance down the road. Focus on getting preapproved, comparing lender offers, and understanding what monthly payment works for your budget.

    Recent findings suggest that nerdWallet’s affordability calculator can help you estimate your potential monthly payment. If a fresh home isn’t in the cards right now, there are still things you can do to strengthen your buyer profile. Take this time to pay down existing debts and build your down payment savings. Not only will this free up more cash flow for a future mortgage payment, it can also get you a better interest rate when you’re ready to buy.

    Rate locks protect you from increases while your loan is processed, and with the market forever bouncing around, that peace of mind can be worth it.

    It has been revealed that berkshire Hathaway (BRKA -0.47%) (BRKB -0.36%), under the direction of Warren Buffett, began buying Apple (AAPL -1.90%) shares in the first quarter of 2016. That investment has worked out extremely well. At one point, the Cupertino tech giant accounted for 50% of the conglomerate's portfolio.

    Even after trimming the position from fourth-quarter 2023 through the end of 2025, as of Nov. 17, the ”Magnificent Seven” stock represented 25% of Berkshire Hathaway's total public equity portfolio, and it is still its largest holding. The number of shares remained unchanged this year. This was despite there being a lot of shuffling among other positions.

    Here's what Berkshire holding on to the Apple stake tells investors.

    Industry observers note that over the three-month period from the start of July to the end of September, Apple shares traded at an average price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 36.8. Any rational investor would call this an expensive stock. That's doubly true for those who see equities through a value-focused lens. The share price has moved 29% higher in 2026.

    Industry observers note that berkshire Hathaway didn't sell a single share during the third quarter. This might come as a surprise to those who have followed the diversified corporation's actions in recent years.

    Warren Buffett oversaw the selling of Apple shares over multiple quarters from the end of 2023 to the end of 2025. For example, during the second quarter of 2024, when the technology stock traded at an average P/E multiple of 29, much lower than what it sells for today, Berkshire Hathaway cut its position dramatically.

    While the single holding had become a significant part of the portfolio, it's fair to assume that valuation played a part in these decisions. Now, with a P/E ratio that's approaching 40, it looks like less emphasis is being placed on the valuation being an influential factor.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Sources indicate that greg Abel has been the chief executive officer of Berkshire Hathaway since the start of 2026. He has made notable moves in his short tenure thus far, but as outside observers, we have zero clue what he and Warren Buffett are discussing regarding the conglomerate's capital allocation strategy. All we can do is try to come up with some takeaways.

    Staying true to Warren Buffett's investing philosophy, the Apple position is a clear signal that Berkshire Hathaway will hold on to its winners and let them run. "When we own portions of outstanding businesses with outstanding managements, our favorite holding period is forever," Buffett wrote in his 1988 shareholder letter.

    The iPhone maker has been in the portfolio for nearly 11 years. Given how much of the market is driven by short-term behavior these days, that time horizon seems like an eternity.

    If Berkshire Hathaway did sell some of its Apple shares in Q3, it wouldn't know where to move that capital. This is a persistent problem. Compared to the hundreds of billions of dollars on the balance sheet that earn low yields, an expensive Apple stock still offers the potential for higher returns. This benefits Berkshire Hathaway shareholders.

    In a recent development, valuation should always be viewed separately from the underlying business. In this instance, Berkshire Hathaway's inactivity is a vote of confidence in the quality of Apple's operations.

    It's hard to dispute that the consumer tech juggernaut is one of the finest companies we've ever seen. A valuable brand, ongoing pricing power, customer loyalty, and innovative DNA are attractive traits. There's also its incredible financial performance, shown by a fiscal 2026 free cash flow margin of 28%.

    College Scholarship Breakdown: Types, Sponsors and Eligibility at a Glance

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1394 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, scholarships have become a standard part of applying for college.
    • Before you go searching for a scholarship, it's notable to understand the types of scholarships available and how to identify the ones that give you the best chance of winning, which can save you time and potentially earn you more funding.
    • According to recent reports, scholarships are often funded by three groups: private organizations, institutions like universities, and government agencies.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, scholarships have become a standard part of applying for college. You can learn about scholarships in a variety of ways, but looking through an online database of available scholarships — the most common way — can be overwhelming.

    Before you go searching for a scholarship, it's notable to understand the types of scholarships available and how to identify the ones that give you the best chance of winning, which can save you time and potentially earn you more funding. Here’s what you need to know about scholarships to decide which ones are best for you.

    According to recent reports, scholarships are often funded by three groups: private organizations, institutions like universities, and government agencies. None is better than the other when it comes to awarding funds.

    Nonprofit organizations and clubs that are looking for students either majoring in or researching certain fields, or who have experience volunteering in a specific field.

    Companies that want to support all students or only fund those majoring in a field that relates to the companies’ industries.

    Financial institutions, such as banks or credit unions, that want to support their community or their members.

    Individuals or families that are funding private scholarships, usually in memory of a loved one.

    Universities and colleges that are offering funds to students who attend their campuses.

    Research organizations that want to fund students who will research in their areas of interest and further their causes.

    These scholarships generally are provided by local, state or federal government agencies for a variety of reasons. Despite being funded by a government agency, the scholarships do not require you to pay back the money — unlike federal student loans.

    Some scholarships pay for anything related to college expenses, including tuition, room and board, books and supplies, and more. Other scholarships limit what you can pay for with the funds, such as only tuition or tuition along with books. It’s important to look at this restriction when applying for scholarships to ensure the funds will go toward what you need to cover.

    In a recent development, merit scholarships require you to show excellence or achievements in your schoolwork, through talents and abilities, and even leadership or service work. Because these types of awards can be highly competitive, merit scholarships might require more than just achievements, such as volunteer or leadership experience. This means merit-based scholarships can overlap with other types of scholarship categories. Here are some examples of merit-based scholarships:.

    Merit scholarships often require you to have earned a minimum grade point average (GPA). The minimum GPA depends on the scholarship but often ranges from 2.0 to 4.0, with more competitive scholarships usually requiring higher GPAs. Scholarships with lower GPA minimums are more likely to consider additional factors, such as financial need.

    Some merit scholarships might require a minimum ACT or SAT score instead of a GPA — or in addition to a minimum GPA.

    In a recent development, merit scholarships might also require applicants to have participated in activities outside of their schoolwork. This is common for scholarships that require membership in a certain group or organization. For example, membership in agricultural clubs, such as 4-H or FFA, and scouting groups, such as the National Eagle Scout Association, appear in scholarship requirements.

    Industry observers note that some scholarships emphasize volunteering or community service and only consider applicants who have that experience. Applications vary in how detailed their requirements can be. Some scholarships want only a general description of where and how you’ve volunteered, and others might require experience with a service project that shows more leadership experience or time volunteering with a certain type of organization.

    Scholarships that are awarded to students who can’t afford college are called need-based scholarships.

    Unmet financial need is the difference between what it will cost you to attend college and what you can afford to pay. Because calculating how much you can afford is a complicated process, many scholarships refer to your FAFSA to document your financial need.

    It has been revealed that some scholarship requirements may be as straightforward as demonstrating that you have financial need, but some scholarships might have income limits. However, income restrictions are less common.

    Sources indicate that athletic scholarships are for — you guessed it — athletes. They are usually offered by colleges and universities to recruit athletes onto their collegiate teams and can be competitive. Which sports have scholarships available and the scholarship amounts vary by college.

    It has been revealed that even though the main criterion for an athletic scholarship is being good at your sport, you’ll likely still need to show that you can keep up with your schoolwork. Most athletic scholarships require students to earn a minimum GPA or test scores to remain eligible while they’re in college.

    Sources indicate that some scholarships are designated for students majoring in a general field, such as science or education, but others can be for very specific areas of study. For example, a scholarship for students majoring in a natural resource field could include majors in biology, ecology, wildlife biology, conservation education, forestry, soils and hydrology. However, a stricter scholarship might state that students have to major in more specific topics, such as biochemistry or microbial ecology.

    According to recent reports, scholarships are available for active and former members of the military and members of their families. In addition to federal funds available for veterans to attend college, private organizations and some universities have scholarships for veterans to offset the cost of a degree.

    According to recent reports, which family members can apply for funds depends on the individual scholarship. For example, some scholarships extend to children or spouses of veterans, but some go as far in a family tree as great-grandchildren.

    It has been revealed that veteran- and military-focused scholarships might require that applicants or their family members enlisted in a certain branch, served during a particular time or conflict, or meet a certain rank or status such as receiving disability. Scholarships might also require that the applicant be a wartime veteran or family member of a wartime veteran; not all veterans meet this status.

    Scholarships are also awarded to people who identify with a certain group. Common examples of identity-based scholarships include those for people who have disabilities, belong to certain ethnic or religious groups, identify as LGBTQIA+ or are first-generation students. Some identity-based scholarships require applicants to meet several criteria, such as belonging to more than one identity group.

    Outside of what would be considered standard DEI groups, there are scholarships for applicants who identify with less common groups, such as veganism, homelessness and model railroad builders.

    Recent findings suggest that the best scholarships for you depend on your situation. For example, if you are a skilled athlete with a good academic record, going for an athletic scholarship might give you the most funding. On the other hand, if you’re going to research a topic that isn’t common, looking for scholarships that support your research topic might be your best bet because competition could be lower.

    Good tactics to figure out which scholarships are worth your time include:.

    Recent findings suggest that think of the skills, talents, experience and identities that are unique to you. For example, being a child of a veteran immediately qualifies you for scholarships with fewer applicants than scholarships open to everyone. Likewise, if you embrace a certain ethnicity, identify with a specific group or have experience with a type of work, you might qualify for scholarships that appreciate and recognize those attributes more than the average scholarship.

    Industry observers note that apply if you think you're eligible. Don’t apply to just a few scholarships and hope you get them. Instead, apply for as many scholarships as you can and for which you’re eligible. This increases your chances of receiving funds. Even small scholarships can make a substantial impact when you add several of them together.

    Understand how you can use the money. If you already have a scholarship that covers only books, applying for the same type of scholarship isn’t helpful if you don’t need the extra funds. Instead, look for scholarships that cover the costs you have remaining.

    Not sure where to look? Our sister site Scholarships360.org provides students with vetted scholarship opportunities. That would be a good place to start.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Sara Appino – Updated Nov 22, 2026 at 5:58PM EST.
    • Deciding between established financial research and high-growth payment technology requires a choice between steady market influence and rapid expansion.
    • In a recent development, morningstar provides the critical research and data that power modern investment decisions for millions of retail and institutional consumers.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Sara Appino – Updated Nov 22, 2026 at 5:58PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Morningstar ›.

    Deciding between established financial research and high-growth payment technology requires a choice between steady market influence and rapid expansion. Is Morningstar (MORN -0.30%) or Sezzle (SEZL -6.09%) the better buy today?

    In a recent development, morningstar provides the critical research and data that power modern investment decisions for millions of retail and institutional consumers. Conversely, Sezzle is a disruptor in the payments space, offering flexible financing options for younger consumers. While both operate in the financial world, they cater to different market segments with unique risk and reward profiles.

    In a recent development, morningstar sells investment insights, data, and technology tools to a massive audience, including roughly 4.2 million individual investors and 425,000 financial advisors. The tech giant serves eight primary customer groups, ranging from retirement plan providers and wealth managers to asset managers and fixed-income security issuers. Recently, it has integrated artificial intelligence through partnerships with major technology firms to automate analytics and improve user experience.

    In a recent development, in the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached nearly $2.6 billion, representing revenue growth of approximately 9.4%. This expansion helped the company achieve net income of close to $445.5 million during the same period. The steady climb in both top and bottom lines suggests consistent demand for the company's proprietary financial data and research services.

    As of its September 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is roughly 1.8x (or 1.6x excluding operating lease liabilities). This ratio, which compares total debt to shareholder equity, reflects an increase in financial leverage after the company took on additional debt to fund acquisitions and share repurchases. The current ratio, which measures a company's ability to cover its short-term debts with short-term assets, is approximately 1.05x. In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, free cash flow reached nearly $492.8 million (following $442.6 million in fiscal year 2025).

    Industry observers note that sezzle operates a platform that allows consumers to finance purchases at the point of sale. It focuses heavily on Gen Z and Millennial shoppers, connecting them with a vast network of merchants to increase average order values. By integrating with e-commerce platforms, the manufacturer captures a growing slice of the fintech stocks landscape.

    In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached approximately $581.6 million, marking significant revenue growth of nearly 38.9%. This surge in activity led to a net income of close to $182.6 million for the period. The company also maintained a strong net margin of roughly 31.4% during this high-growth phase, indicating it is generating significant profit from its revenue.

    As of its September 2026 balance sheet, the current ratio stands at approximately 4.2x, suggesting a robust ability to cover immediate liabilities. The debt-to-equity ratio is roughly 0.4x, meaning its total debt is less than half of its shareholder equity. In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, free cash flow reached nearly $297.6 million, providing the manufacturer with substantial capital to reinvest in its growth and fund share repurchases.

    Morningstar faces risks tied to its reputation, as any perceived conflict of interest in its credit ratings or research could damage its brand. Its business is sensitive to market volatility, which can reduce asset-based fees when total market values decline. The company also competes with major data providers such as S&P Global (NYSE:SPGI) and MSCI (MSCI -2.22%) in the institutional research space.

    In a recent development, sezzle relies heavily on a single originating bank partner, WebBank, for the majority of its loans, which creates a significant concentration risk. It faces intense competition in the payment sector and ongoing regulatory scrutiny regarding consumer lending practices and interest rates. Additionally, antitrust litigation involving partners like Shopify (SHOP -6.25%) could indirectly impact its growth trajectory or existing merchant relationships.

    According to recent reports, morningstar offers a more conservative entry point based on its sales, while Sezzle carries a higher premium that reflects its faster growth and superior net margin. The Forward P/E ratio compares a organization's share price to its future earnings estimates, while the P/S ratio measures market value against sales over the past twelve months.

    Valuation metrics include sourcing from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from other data providers.

    In a recent development, but there are some risks that give me pause: Sezzle lends to shoppers, so bad loans matter. Its newest products start with higher losses, and regulators and a lawsuit against Shopify add costs and uncertainty.

    Morningstar, a trusted name in investing research, carries less credit risk, and its stock costs less relative to expected earnings. Its operating profit jumped last quarter, but sales growth is modest. Ultimately, I like that Sezzle is already profitable and still early in its expansion, with room to add new services. If you're investing for the long haul and can handle some risk, Sezzle's fast-growing payments platform looks like the better buy for 2027.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that upstart's (UPST -7.88%) days as a hot fintech stock have long since passed.
    • While shares in this artificial intelligence (AI) lending technology firm have seen brief partial rebounds in recent years, I’m looking more closely at fintech names with stronger growth stories, namely SoFi Technologies (SOFI -7.76%).
    • According to recent reports, at first glance, it may seem illogical that Upstart continues to tumble.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Thomas Niel – Nov 22, 2026 at 6:04PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than SoFi Technologies ›.

    Sources indicate that upstart's (UPST -7.88%) days as a hot fintech stock have long since passed. It was trading near $400 per share back in 2021, but recently was changing hands for around $17 per share, a nearly 96% price decline.

    While shares in this artificial intelligence (AI) lending technology firm have seen brief partial rebounds in recent years, I’m looking more closely at fintech names with stronger growth stories, namely SoFi Technologies (SOFI -7.76%).

    According to recent reports, at first glance, it may seem illogical that Upstart continues to tumble. After all, following steep revenue declines in 2023 and 2024, sales and earnings have improved dramatically. In 2024, revenue and earnings per share (EPS) came in at $628.8 million and -$1.44, respectively. In 2025, revenue surged to just over $1 billion, with diluted EPS at $0.45 per share, marking a massive swing back to profitability.

    For 2026, analysts' estimates call for Upstart to report $1.35 billion in sales and EPS of $1.84. Alas, there is a reason the market prices Upstart at such a low multiple to those estimates.

    First, there is high uncertainty over future growth. Although the company recently reported a 34% increase in quarterly revenue to $371 million, and diluted earnings of $0.33 per share, up 43.4% from the prior year's quarter, management walked back its full-year guidance. Previously estimating  $1.4 billion in revenue and adjusted EBITDA of $294 million, Upstart's full-year 2026 outlook now calls for $1.32 billion in revenue and adjusted EBITDA of $260 million.

    Recent findings suggest that second, the recent pullback in AI stocks and tech stocks has likely intensified the situation. This sell-off has spilled over into the fintech space, including shares in SoFi, a tech giant more richly priced than Upstart but with far greater long-term upside potential.

    Sources indicate that like Upstart, SoFi has recently reported strong growth. Last quarter, the digital-first financial services organization reported net revenue of $1.4 billion, a 44% increase from the prior year's quarter. Adjusted EBITDA jumped 70% year over year, to $470 million. EPS came in at $0.18, a 63% increase from the $0.11 in diluted adjusted EPS reported for Q3 2025.

    Better yet, SoFi's management provided bullish guidance for the coming year. In 2027, the manufacturer anticipates 27% adjusted net revenue growth and adjusted earnings of $0.90 per share, adding that it could achieve these goals without raising additional capital. With SoFi Technologies changing hands today at around $13.50 per share, the stock is trading at around 15 times next year's estimated earnings.

    Longer-term, if SoFi can continue to grow at a moderate clip, steadily becoming a major "financial supermarket," shares could climb further, to past highs in the $30s per share, and beyond. Contrast that with Upstart, which, while still guiding for further growth, is revising that guidance downward. Worse yet, although both SoFi and Upstart are involved in the personal lending space, Upstart arguably has greater exposure. SoFi started as a lender but has since expanded into banking, brokerage, and other financial services, with its ability to cross-sell bolstering confidence in its growth story.

    That mentioned, it's still possible for Upstart to thrive while SoFi flounders. The sell-side remains divided on SoFi, perhaps reluctant to assign it a fintech valuation, given that it will eventually be classified as a bank stock. Upstart has tanked on poor guidance, but any sort of better-than-feared results and outlook could be enough to drive a relief rally. Nevertheless, if you're looking at either stock as a possible long-term investment rather than a trade, consider SoFi the better of the two.

    Ray Dalio says Bessent move is sign that a debt crisis is getting closer; recommends gold and bitcoin

    📅 21 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (610 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's debt buyback announcement this week fits into a broader pattern that can signal a forthcoming crisis, according to billionaire investor Ray Dalio.
    • In a recent development, the Bridgewater Associates founder remarked Bessent's proposal to increase government debt purchases may portend trouble for the U.S.
    • "I am confident that the government's financial condition is at an inflection point," Dalio wrote in a LinkedIn post published Friday.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's debt buyback announcement this week fits into a broader pattern that can signal a forthcoming crisis, according to billionaire investor Ray Dalio.

    In a recent development, the Bridgewater Associates founder remarked Bessent's proposal to increase government debt purchases may portend trouble for the U.S. economy. Coupled with the Japanese government reducing its U.S. bond market exposure and surging long-dated American bond yields, Dalio said investors may want to prepare their portfolios for increased risk by owning cryptocurrencies and gold.

    "I am confident that the government's financial condition is at an inflection point," Dalio wrote in a LinkedIn post published Friday. "If this is not dealt with now, the debts will build up to levels where they can't be managed without great trauma.".

    Dalio noted that the Treasury Department has "only limited capacity" to buy back bonds. Bessent told CNBC on Thursday that his team was going to "make a market" and that the purchases would likely top $4 billion.

    According to recent reports, the U.S. is spending about 40% more than it's bringing in, resulting in the burgeoning budget deficit, Dalio noted. The U.S. budget deficit topped $432 billion in July, but Bessent told CNBC that it's likely peaked under President Donald Trump's administration.

    Recent findings suggest that bessent said in the interview that a team was looking at ways to shrink spending by hundreds of billions of dollars. But Dalio said there is "very little ability" to do so given that it is either committed or considered essential.

    After years of overspending, Dalio said total debt now dwarfs what the U.S. brings in each year. If the U.S. government was a business, Dalio said debt service payments would come in at roughly $11 trillion — about 200% of annual revenue.

    Dalio, 77, warned the cost of repaying principal and servicing the debt will only grow over time.

    Sources indicate that to solve this, Dalio noted the U.S. needs to carefully employ a three-part strategy to get the budget deficit down to 3% of gross domestic product.

    According to recent reports, first, Dalio stated the U.S. government needs to reduce its spending. Second, he said tax revenue needs to be raised. Finally, the New York native and Harvard Business School alumni said lower interest rates were needed.

    "All three need to happen concurrently so as to prevent any one from being too large," Dalio said. "If any one is too large, the adjustment will be traumatic.".

    Dalio cautioned against ramming through these adjustments by "force." For instance, "it would be very bad if the Federal Reserve unnaturally forced interest rates down," he mentioned.

    Dalio noted it's vital to to take steps now, while the economy is healthy. An economy in recession requires increased government spending, he said.

    Dalio remarked the exact timing of a debt crisis can be swayed by variables ranging from military conflict to political change. On its current trajectory, the U.S. could enter such a crisis in as early as one year or as late as five. "My guess, which I suppose will be a bad one, is that it will come in three years, give or take two, if the course we're on is not changed.".

    To prepare, Dalio recommended investors are underweight debt assets, such as bonds.

    As much as 10% to 15% of a portfolio could land in gold, as well as "a bit" of bitcoin, the hedge fund founder said.

    Sources indicate that dalio's post came at the tail end of a volatile week for U.S. financial markets. Rising long-term Treasury yields have pressured stocks, leading the S&P 500 to snap a a three-week-long advance.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • This is why you should always wait for evidence before trading on your thesis.
    • Industry observers note that back in June, I started rethinking my bearish outlook on artificial intelligence (AI) voice chatbot specialist SoundHound AI (SOUN -10.31%).
    • In a recent development, since then, its stock has fallen 54%.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By John Bromels – Nov 22, 2026 at 6:50PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than SoundHound AI ›.

    This is why you should always wait for evidence before trading on your thesis.

    Industry observers note that back in June, I started rethinking my bearish outlook on artificial intelligence (AI) voice chatbot specialist SoundHound AI (SOUN -10.31%). I suggested investors should keep an eye on the company.

    In a recent development, since then, its stock has fallen 54%. Over the past year, it's down 75%. Boy, am I glad I didn't recommend buying it in June!

    But at just $3.10 per share (at the time of this writing), has SoundHound's stock price dropped to the point that it's now a buy? It could be ... if SoundHound can make this one thing happen by 2027.

    Industry observers note that what's so strange about the stock's recent performance is that trailing-12-month (TTM) revenue has continued to rise even as the stock price has fallen. Q3 revenue hit a record $62.4 million, bringing TTM revenue to $223.6 million.

    Meanwhile, SoundHound's shares peaked in late 2024 at $24.23 per share. They're now sitting at about $3.10 per share, a 52-week low.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    According to recent reports, management expects revenue to continue improving, with guidance of $350 million to $400 million for 2027. But there's more to that number than meets the eye.

    According to recent reports, soundHound is still digesting its recent acquisition of LivePerson, an enterprise digital messaging platform with significant debt on its balance sheet. SoundHound used an equity raise to retire that debt completely.

    In a recent development, livePerson brought an extensive patent portfolio and existing contracts with major Fortune 100 companies. SoundHound is now integrating LivePerson's messaging infrastructure with its own OASYS agentic voice AI platform to offer an omnichannel customer engagement system that "operates natively across voice, web, mobile, SMS, and social channels.".

    As if this transition weren't enough, SoundHound is also switching to a recurring-revenue, hosted-solution model. This kind of transition is usually a long-term positive for a firm, but can result in lumpy revenue during the transition period.

    It has been revealed that another variable is the high amount of churn among LivePerson customers prior to the acquisition. Plus, because the acquisition didn't close until Sept. 4, LivePerson only contributed about $14 million to SoundHound's Q3 revenue. That means SoundHound's organic revenue growth was just 15.2% year over year (YOY), which is much lower than Q2's 45% growth and Q1's 52% growth.

    For SoundHound to turn around its slumping stock price, it needs to show it can do more than just achieve revenue growth. It needs to make meaningful improvements in the quality of its revenue.

    Cost reductions and synergies with LivePerson will play a role. Management believes it can identify $80 million in annualized cost reductions that will take effect by the end of the calendar year. But the company has also noted that it is exiting some legacy contracts with negative growth margins, which will result in the loss of some lower-quality revenue.

    According to recent reports, ultimately, SoundHound's 2027 revenue guidance implies 68% revenue growth from the past year. The LivePerson acquisition will likely get the company most of the way there. What investors should instead be watching is whether SoundHound's margins and quarterly cash burn improve, how much of its existing revenue is converting to annual recurring revenue, and how well it retains and upsells LivePerson's customer base.

    If SoundHound AI can show meaningful revenue quality improvement by 2027, it will look like a steal at its current share price.

    Arm vs. Marvell Technology: Which Artificial Intelligence Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1078 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Robert Izquierdo – Updated Nov 22, 2026 at 6:50PM EST.
    • Recent findings suggest that the expansion of artificial intelligence has pushed investors toward high-growth hardware providers.
    • Recent findings suggest that arm provides the energy-efficient architecture used in almost every smartphone, while Marvell specializes in high-speed networking and data center infrastructure.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Robert Izquierdo – Updated Nov 22, 2026 at 6:50PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Arm Holdings ›.

    Recent findings suggest that the expansion of artificial intelligence has pushed investors toward high-growth hardware providers. Choosing between Arm Holdings (ARM -14.09%) and Marvell Technology (MRVL -11.69%) requires a careful look at their different roles in the chip ecosystem.

    Recent findings suggest that arm provides the energy-efficient architecture used in almost every smartphone, while Marvell specializes in high-speed networking and data center infrastructure. Both companies are positioned to benefit from the rising demand for accelerated computing, yet they offer distinct risk profiles and valuation levels. This comparison helps you determine which path fits your investment strategy through 2027.

    In a recent development, in the rapidly evolving world of semiconductor stocks, Arm is unique because it did not actually manufacture chips historically. Instead, it designs the primary architecture and licenses its intellectual property. Its energy-efficient designs are in over 99% of smartphones, although the organization is now expanding into cloud data centers and automotive applications, and intends to produce its own chips at last.

    According to recent reports, the company has shifted toward more complete chip designs to command higher royalty rates. This model creates a high-margin recurring revenue stream. Since it serves almost every major chipmaker, it sits at the heart of the tech sector.

    According to recent reports, in the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached $5.5 billion, representing growth of 23.8% compared to the prior year. This expansion is supported by the adoption of its latest v9 architecture, which carries higher royalty rates than previous generations. The company reported net income of $936.0 million during this period.

    As of its March 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was 0.1x. This ratio compares total debt to shareholder equity to help you understand how much a company relies on borrowing. The current ratio, which measures the ability to pay short-term obligations with current assets, was a robust 6.0x.

    It has been revealed that in the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026, free cash flow reached $979.0 million. Free cash flow is the cash remaining after a business pays for operations and equipment. Note that stock-based compensation (SBC) represented roughly 69% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

    It has been revealed that marvell focuses on the infrastructure that makes modern data centers and telecommunications networks possible. The organization specializes in data processing units, networking silicon, and storage controllers. Its recent growth is driven by the need for high-speed connectivity between servers in artificial intelligence clusters.

    It has been revealed that the tech giant faces significant customer concentration, as its ten largest customers represented roughly 82% of net revenue in its latest annual report. One distributor accounted for approximately 37% of sales, which adds a layer of risk to the business. Despite this, its specialized silicon is vital for major cloud service providers.

    In the 12 months ended Aug. 1, 2026, revenue reached $9.5 billion. This reflects a growth rate of 30.6% over the previous twelve-month period. During this same window, the tech giant generated net income of $2.6 billion, showing significant improvement from previous years.

    Recent findings suggest that as of its January 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was 0.3x, indicating a low reliance on debt. The current ratio stood at roughly 2.0x, indicating a healthy ability to meet short-term financial commitments.

    Recent findings suggest that in the fiscal year ended Jan. 31, 2026, free cash flow was $1.4 billion. Note that stock-based compensation represented roughly 33.8% of operating cash flow.

    Industry observers note that arm faces risks related to the concentration of the smartphone market. If global phone sales slow, its royalty revenue could stagnate. The manufacturer also competes with open-source alternatives like RISC-V, which some manufacturers may prefer to avoid licensing fees. Furthermore, its heavy reliance on the licensing model means any loss of key partnerships with giants like Nvidia (NVDA -14.01%) or Qualcomm (QCOM -7.45%) could impact its long-term growth prospects.

    Sources indicate that marvell Technology deals with significant customer concentration and geopolitical uncertainty. Trade restrictions and export controls regarding China have created supply chain challenges and impacted demand. The firm is also navigating a massive $115 billion all-stock acquisition of Lumentum Holdings (LITE -13.94%), which carries integration risks and potential shareholder dilution. Additionally, it recently settled patent litigation with Credo Technology Group Holding (CRDO -15.20%), highlighting the constant legal threats in the specialized silicon market.

    Marvell Technology appears more attractive on a valuation basis, offering lower Forward P/E and P/S ratio multiples than Arm.

    Valuation metrics include sourcing from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from other data providers.

    For investors seeking exposure to the artificial intelligence boom, Arm and Marvell are two compelling stocks to own. Between the two, I would prioritize picking up shares of Marvell going into 2027.

    Marvell sports a much lower share price valuation than Arm, providing a greater opportunity for a superior return. Arm arguably deserves the elevated valuation multiples because of its high-margin licensing moat. However, given its foray into making its own semiconductor chips, it risks compressing those robust margins due to manufacturing costs.

    Marvell's stock was beaten down after it announced it was acquiring Lumentum. I think the acquisition is a smart move. Lumentum provides high-speed optical capabilities for transferring massive amounts of data, a key competitive advantage to winning AI customers. The appeal of Lumentum's solutions is illustrated by its sales of $1.3 billion for its fiscal first quarter, ended Sept. 26, which represented 137% year-over-year growth.

    Moreover, Marvell's business is exploding. It generated revenue of $8.2 billion in its 2026 fiscal year, ended Jan. 31, 2026, and the company expects sales to soar to a range between $70 billion to $90 billion by its 2031 fiscal year. That growth does not include Lumentum's sales. With a lower valuation and spectacular, multi-year growth ahead, Marvell looks like the better stock to buy now.

    Berkshire Hathaway's Next Substantial AI Bet Could Be Hiding in Plain Sight

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (797 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Reuben Gregg Brewer – Nov 22, 2026 at 7:15PM EST.
    • 10 stocks we like better than Berkshire Hathaway ›.
    • Sources indicate that berkshire Hathaway (BRKA -0.47%)(BRKB -0.36%) isn't exactly seen as an artificial intelligence (AI) play.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Reuben Gregg Brewer – Nov 22, 2026 at 7:15PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Berkshire Hathaway ›.

    Sources indicate that berkshire Hathaway (BRKA -0.47%)(BRKB -0.36%) isn't exactly seen as an artificial intelligence (AI) play. But it may have more exposure to this emerging technology than you realize. In fact, the company's large utility and energy operations present opportunities for AI-related investment that are hiding in plain sight. Here's what you need to know and what Berkshire Hathaway could easily do to increase its AI bets.

    According to recent reports, berkshire Hathaway is usually classified as a finance business, which isn't a bad place to put it. After all, it has large insurance operations. However, the company is really a massive conglomerate, with businesses including insurance, utilities, energy, manufacturing, housing, and retail, to provide just a short list and high-level view. In Greg Abel's first annual letter as CEO, he reported that the company had 51 non-insurance operating businesses. In a previous letter, former CEO Warren Buffett mentioned the company owned 189 operating businesses. The definition of an operating business is probably responsible for the two different numbers, but either one you pick, the number is huge.

    It has been revealed that greg Abel. Image source: Getty Images.

    There is a lot hiding inside Berkshire Hathaway. But, notably, it breaks out a few large businesses, including railroads, utilities, and energy. The last two are increasingly tied to the artificial intelligence industry. The company's utility operations provide the electricity that powers AI. The energy business helps supply the natural gas that lets utilities, and increasingly AI companies, generate electricity.

    Recent findings suggest that to be fair, Berkshire Hathaway could easily afford to buy a technology business with its cash hoard of more than $370 billion. Only technology isn't really the type of business that Berkshire Hathaway tends to buy. Former CEO Warren Buffett long focused on acquiring boring businesses that were well run and attractively priced at the time of purchase. For example, trains, utilities, and pipelines. Greg Abel's acquisition of homebuilder Taylor Morrison Home for $8.5 billion suggests he's not going to suddenly shift directions.

    Sources indicate that it would be exciting if Berkshire Hathaway went out and bought a giant U.S. utility, such as NextEra Energy (NEE -0.41%), or a large pipeline business, such as Enterprise Products Partners (EPD -0.91%). While Greg Abel probably wouldn't target companies of that scale, the CEO could certainly afford to buy smaller players in either sector.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    But that's not necessary. Both the utility and midstream sectors are capital intensive. Utilities own massive power plants that take years to build and require huge sums of money. Midstream companies are no different, with their pipelines, storage, refineries, and transportation assets. It isn't unusual for a utility or midstream manufacturer to have multi-billion-dollar capital investment prepares extending as far as five years into the future.

    What that means is Berkshire Hathaway could make very large capital investments within its existing operations. And that, in fact, is probably the most likely outcome. The cash on the company's balance sheet, meanwhile, means it could easily afford the required spending. Speaking to the utility and energy segment, Greg Abel noted at the start of 2026 that, "Infrastructure built for hyperscalers and data centers must be paid for by those customers and reflect the risks tied to step-changes in long-term demand." Increasingly, data center operators appear willing to do just that.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    According to recent reports, for example, Chevron (CVX +0.91%), a longtime holding in Berkshire Hathaway's stock portfolio, has agreed to build a power plant that will use Chevron-produced natural gas to supply dedicated power to data centers. Berkshire Hathaway could do something similar with relative ease.

    According to recent reports, berkshire Hathaway is unlikely to start buying up AI technology businesses. That's just not what the company does. However, if you dig into the conglomerate's operations, you see that it still has material opportunity to invest in the AI sector. And while it would be exciting if Greg Abel augmented the company's utility and energy operations through new acquisitions, it is far more likely that Berkshire Hathaway will simply invest in its own operations to benefit from AI growth over time. That's the opportunity that is hiding in plain sight.

    Stifel Says SpaceX Could Buy Stalled Data Centers for One Reason: Their Power. Here’s Why Electricity Is the Real Asset.

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (940 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Reuben Gregg Brewer – Nov 22, 2026 at 8:01PM EST.
    • Industry observers note that wall Street analysts can only make educated guesses, just like every other investor.
    • In a recent development, the key theme, however, is that SpaceX will likely only be interested in data centers that already have dedicated power.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Reuben Gregg Brewer – Nov 22, 2026 at 8:01PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Bloom Energy ›.

    Industry observers note that wall Street analysts can only make educated guesses, just like every other investor. But they do have an advantage since they are often industry experts. This is why Stifel analyst Jonathan Siegmann's suggestion that Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX -7.69%) could buy up stalled data centers is so interesting.

    In a recent development, the key theme, however, is that SpaceX will likely only be interested in data centers that already have dedicated power. Here's why this is so notable and what it could mean for your stock selection process as you look at companies like Bloom Energy (BE -15.30%), NextEra Energy (NEE -0.41%), and Brookfield Renewable (BEP -2.97%).

    Industry observers note that spaceX has a large AI data center in Memphis that it has dubbed Colossus. It is a huge asset, and it uses massive amounts of power. To ensure there is enough electricity to run the data center, SpaceX built its own dedicated natural-gas power plant. Local residents aren't happy about this, but it highlights that SpaceX is clearly aware of the power problem posed by AI data centers.

    It has been revealed that as the backlash against AI data centers grows, access to electricity is becoming an increasingly important and contentious problem. Which is why Stifel analyst Jonathan Siegmann thinks SpaceX could end up buying data centers that have dedicated power agreements in place. However, you don't need to play this specific angle to benefit. Increasingly, AI companies are being forced to supply their own power. And there are a handful of companies that look set to benefit, including Bloom Energy, NextEra Energy, and Brookfield Renewable.

    Sources indicate that bloom Energy makes hydrogen fuel cells. Notably, each fuel cell it sells comes along with a long-term service contract, creating an annuity-like income stream. The company's products are factory-built and can be easily deployed wherever they are needed, providing off-grid power. The company has been losing money for years but is likely to be profitable in 2026. That could be an key inflection point for the business.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    But investors are well aware of the opportunity, pushing the stock higher by more than 1,200% over the past three years. With a lofty price-to-earnings ratio of roughly 100x, it is very clearly a well-loved stock. And yet, the opportunity to power AI data centers remains substantial, and perhaps only getting larger. If you are an aggressive growth investor, you should at least consider Bloom Energy, even if you only end up adding it to your wish list.

    It has been revealed that nextEra Energy is one of the world's largest utilities. In fact, it is looking to get even bigger, with its proposed acquisition of Dominion Energy (D -0.56%). Notably, Dominion's regulated electricity operations include one of the world's most important data center markets. The pairing will also vault NextEra into the number two spot with regard to U.S. nuclear power generation. Basically, NextEra looks like it is doubling down on electricity demand and AI at the same time.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    But there's an interesting twist here. NextEra is well positioned to benefit from data centers that get attached to the grid. However, it is also one of the world's largest producers of solar and wind power, a business that falls outside of the regulated framework. So it can also sell power directly to AI customers under long-term contracts. For more conservative investors, NextEra could be an attractive way to play AI's power demand, both from within and outside the regulated framework. You'll also get to collect NextEra's well-above-market 2.9% dividend yield.

    According to recent reports, for investors looking to maximize the income they generate, Brookfield Renewable and its 5.2% may be even more attractive. The partnership is focused on clean energy, but has a surprisingly diversified portfolio. For starters, it operates hydroelectric, solar, and wind power facilities. It has increasingly been investing in battery storage. And it owns half of Westinghouse, which is one of the world's largest service providers to the nuclear power industry. On top of that, it is also geographically diversified, with assets located in North America, South America, Europe, and Asia. It is a one-stop shop for investors seeking a focused clean-energy investment and for customers seeking renewable energy.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Recent findings suggest that the key here, however, is that Brookfield Renewable largely sells power under long-term contracts outside of the regulated framework. It already has large deals with AI giants Microsoft (MSFT -2.77%) and Google. Add in the goal of at least 5% annual distribution growth, and income lovers would be remiss if they didn't at least examine Brookfield Renewable and the AI opportunity ahead of it.

    If you think Stifel analyst Jonathan Siegmann is on to something, you could simply buy SpaceX. That's fine, but it isn't the only takeaway from his insight.     #130924. The 'debasement trade' returns after Bessent bond maneuver. Crypto and gold are back in style

    📅 25 Aug 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (883 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    The 'debasement trade' returns after Bessent bond maneuver. Crypto and gold are back in style

    📅 25 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (883 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The debasement trade is gaining newly introduced traction on Wall Street as concern over the size and cost of the budget deficit mounts.
    • It has been revealed that the conventional wisdom behind the trade is that perceived hard assets, like cryptocurrencies and precious metals, gain as investors try to hedge against a weaker U.S.
    • "The size of the Treasury purchases revealed so far by Bessent are trivial in comparison to the size of the overall market, but the [signaling] effect was very powerful," noted Stephen Coltman, head of macro at 21Shares, a crypto-focused creator of exchange-traded funds.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The debasement trade is gaining newly introduced traction on Wall Street as concern over the size and cost of the budget deficit mounts.

    It has been revealed that the conventional wisdom behind the trade is that perceived hard assets, like cryptocurrencies and precious metals, gain as investors try to hedge against a weaker U.S. dollar and Treasury debt in the face of ballooning government spending. Those fears reached a fever pitch last week before, and after, the Treasury Department's unusual step of increasing debt buybacks under Secretary Scott Bessent.

    "The size of the Treasury purchases revealed so far by Bessent are trivial in comparison to the size of the overall market, but the [signaling] effect was very powerful," noted Stephen Coltman, head of macro at 21Shares, a crypto-focused creator of exchange-traded funds.

    Sources indicate that gold touched three-month highs Monday, building on last week's advance of more than 5%. The yellow metal has climbed for five straight weeks and in August is on track for its biggest monthly rise since 1999.

    It has been revealed that bitcoin added 2% Monday, to the highest since May. Last week, the digital currency soared 22%, its biggest three-day rally since 2023. Overnight Tuesday, the crypto touched $80,000.

    Conversely, investors fled the dollar.

    The U.S. dollar index, which tracks the dollar against six other leading currencies, hit three-month lows last week and recorded its third down week in the last four. The index was little changed on Monday as investors expressed little appetite to bid up the greenback.

    The Treasury Department said last week that it would double the maximum size of its bond buyback, to at least $4 billion from $2 billion. Two senior Treasury officials told CNBC Monday that the department could use its General Account to help fund the prepares.

    In a recent development, last week's announcement followed news that the monthly U.S. budget deficit in July reached a five-year high and came at the same time as total federal government debt topped $40 trillion. Bessent told CNBC last week that he wields a "major toolkit" to calm the government bond market amid concerns about the government's financial health.

    In a recent development, long-dated U.S. Treasury yields surged last week, at one point sending the 30-year yield to almost a 20-year high of 5.34%, up from 4.82% in late June. Yields dipped and then rebounded in the wake of the Treasury buyback move, a signal that bond investors believed Bessent's moves were inadequate.

    It has been revealed that "Markets are saying something," the billionaire philanthropist and former energy trader John Arnold said in a Friday post on X. The weaker dollar, lower Treasury prices and strengthening hard assets, are "all part of the debasement trade," he wrote.

    The Treasury's moves could aid the bond market, but also translate into outsized pain for the dollar, according to Nohshad Shah, Citadel Securities' head of fixed income sales for Europe, the Middle East and Africa.

    It has been revealed that the stakes are high for monetary policymakers, as a weaker greenback can ease financial conditions, Shah said. U.S. inflation — above the Federal Reserve's 2% target for five years — could worsen.

    Industry observers note that the Fed might need to hike interest rates in response, Shah mentioned. Fed funds futures reflect about a 56% chance the central bank raises borrowing costs at its October meeting, up more than seven percentage points from a week ago, according to CME's FedWatch tool.

    It has been revealed that "The bond market's message is straightforward: fiscal or monetary policy should be tighter," Shah stated in a Monday note. "Households may ultimately pay for policymakers' unwillingness to fix the roof whilst the sun is shining.".

    Sources indicate that coltman at 21Shares said the appetite for alternative stores of value also stems from mounting geopolitical tension. The U.S. on Monday rolled out a global sanctions program focused on segregating Iran from the global economy, days after slapping 50% tariffs on billions of dollars in Canadian exports.

    Still, assets that would benefit from a debasement trade have recently received votes of confidence on Wall Street.

    Industry observers note that deutsche Bank analyst Michael Hsueh mentioned in a Monday note that gold could surpass his target price of $4,800 an ounce. Already, that level suggests the precious metal only need to rise another 3% or so from where it closed on Friday. "We see the Treasury policy change as underlining the gold constructive view," Hsueh said.

    According to recent reports, billionaire investor Ray Dalio recommended investors remain overweight gold and bitcoin ahead of what he warned could become a debt crisis in the U.S. as a result of unchecked government spending. Gold could account for as much as 15% of a model portfolio, the Bridgewater Associates founder stated.

    It has been revealed that "The government's financial condition is at an inflection point," Dalio wrote on LinkedIn Friday. "If this is not dealt with now, the debts will build up to levels where they can't be managed without great trauma.".

    Others are less sure, devaluing the notion of a debasement trade.

    It's probably too early to endorse the idea unless it's clear that the Fed will go along with the Treasury Department, stated Alexander Lis, investing chief at Social Discovery Ventures.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Robert Izquierdo – Updated Nov 22, 2026 at 8:03PM EST.
    • Industry observers note that connectivity serves as the backbone of the modern economy, but choosing between infrastructure and services requires careful analysis.
    • According to recent reports, nokia focuses on the hardware and software that make networks run, while AT&T is a retail giant providing wireless and fiber service to millions.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Robert Izquierdo – Updated Nov 22, 2026 at 8:03PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Nokia ›.

    Industry observers note that connectivity serves as the backbone of the modern economy, but choosing between infrastructure and services requires careful analysis. Investing in Nokia Oyj (NOK -8.27%) or AT&T (T +2.10%) involves balancing network equipment growth against steady subscription revenue.

    According to recent reports, nokia focuses on the hardware and software that make networks run, while AT&T is a retail giant providing wireless and fiber service to millions. This comparison examines their business models, balance sheets, and valuations to determine which stock is better for your portfolio.

    Nokia is a global connectivity infrastructure company that builds networks across fixed, mobile, IP, optical, and data center systems. The company serves communications service providers, governments, and large enterprises while operating in approximately 130 countries with roughly 78,000 employees. No single customer accounts for more than 10% of revenue, which helps diversify its revenue streams across various regions and sectors.

    Recent findings suggest that in the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached $22.6 billion, representing revenue growth of 4.1%. The company reported net income of $858.1 million during this period. This growth reflects ongoing investments in network technology as service providers around the world continue to upgrade their existing infrastructure.

    Sources indicate that as of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was 0.2x, indicating a low level of total debt relative to shareholder equity. The current ratio of 1.6x indicates the company has more than enough assets to cover its short-term liabilities. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow was $1.6 billion, which is the cash remaining after operating costs and equipment spending.

    Industry observers note that in the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached $128.9 billion, supported by revenue growth of 3.5%. The company generated net income of $13.1 billion, resulting in a net margin of 10.2%. This net margin represents the percentage of revenue that remains as profit after all expenses are paid.

    It has been revealed that as of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was 1.6x, measuring its total debt against shareholder equity. The current ratio was 0.9x. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow reached $19.4 billion, providing significant capital for dividends and network upgrades.

    According to recent reports, nokia must contend with intense competition from other global equipment providers in an industry with high research and development requirements. Rapid technological shifts in the 5G and upcoming 6G markets mean the manufacturer must constantly innovate to maintain its market share. Geopolitical tensions also carry risks of influencing where the company can deploy its critical national infrastructure projects.

    Industry observers note that AT&T faces significant risks from increasing competition in the wireless and broadband sectors, particularly from cable providers and businesses like EchoStar (ECHO -8.72%). The company is vulnerable to supply chain disruptions and inflationary pressures on network equipment costs. It also faces potential legal liabilities from lead-clad cables and risks associated with labor union contract negotiations for 43% of its workforce.

    AT&T appears more attractively valued based on its lower earnings multiple, while Nokia offers a significantly more conservative balance sheet profile.

    Valuation metrics include sourcing from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from other data providers.

    Weighing whether to invest in Nokia or AT&T comes down to a trade-off between the former's shift toward artificial intelligence infrastructure and balance sheet cleanliness versus the latter's predictable cash flow and higher dividend income. AT&T is the better fit for conservative investors prioritizing passive income and a more attractive valuation.

    Industry observers note that however, I would buy Nokia for 2027. While AT&T sports a robust dividend yield of about 5%, it has not raised its dividend payment since cutting the amount in 2022. It also holds a lot of debt, as evidenced by its debt-to-equity ratio of 1.6x.

    Sources indicate that nokia has the stronger balance sheet, and its focus on AI infrastructure is paying off. In the third quarter, AI and cloud sales soared 123% and customer orders rose 118% year over year.

    According to recent reports, nokia's AI radio access network (AI-RAN) technology uses artificial intelligence to intelligently manage traffic on 5G networks for better speed, coverage, and capacity. AI-RAN is still being tested but is approaching commercial deployment. Thanks to its artificial intelligence business, Nokia stock has a higher potential for share price appreciation than AT&T.

    Latest Update: With the Nasdaq in a Correction, Vanguard's Tech ETF Is the Fund I'd Buy Now

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (892 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • 10 stocks we like better than Vanguard Information Technology ETF ›.
    • It has been revealed that the tech sell-off that started in October has become a correction.
    • Recent findings suggest that the Vanguard Information Technology ETF (VGT -7.00%) has dropped even more.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Daniel Sparks – Nov 22, 2026 at 8:23PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Vanguard Information Technology ETF ›.

    It has been revealed that the tech sell-off that started in October has become a correction. As I write, the Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC -5.28%) has dropped around 13% from its all-time closing high, hit on Oct. 6.

    Recent findings suggest that the Vanguard Information Technology ETF (VGT -7.00%) has dropped even more. It finished at $104.99 on Nov. 19, its lowest close since May 4 and around 19% below its own Oct. 6 record of $129.80.

    That said, the fund's still up around 12% in 2026 as of this writing, counting dividends.

    Recent findings suggest that when the fund was about 10% below its peak in late October, I didn't think it was a bargain yet. At today's price, I do.

    The businesses in it have kept growing their earnings as the share price dropped, and I'd be glad to pay the resulting valuation for a fund I proposal to hold for years to come.

    The fund owns 315 stocks, but a handful of them drive it. As of Oct. 31, Apple was around 18% of its assets, Nvidia (NVDA -14.01%) about 17%, and Microsoft about 12%.

    These three haven't moved in step. Apple stock is within about 2% of its record as of this writing. Nvidia, though, has fallen about 29% since Oct. 30 alone. By my math, Nvidia by itself is behind about half of the fund's 10% fall since then.

    According to recent reports, the slide came with a leadership change. Nvidia mentioned on Nov. 12 that Jensen Huang had resigned as CEO, with CFO Colette Kress taking over as interim CEO. On Nov. 19, California's attorney general followed with an investigative subpoena over whether Nvidia's advanced chips or confidential information might have gone to China, and if the tech giant misled investors about that risk.

    But Nvidia's business is still booming. In the third quarter of its fiscal 2027 (the period ending Oct. 25), the company's revenue more than doubled year over year to $115.8 billion. Data center revenue climbed 110%, and non-GAAP (adjusted) earnings per share surged 111%. Management also forecast fiscal fourth-quarter revenue of about $130 billion.

    In other words, much of the fund's fall has come from investors paying less for the same chip profits, not from those profits dropping.

    Vanguard lists the average price-to-earnings ratio of the stocks in the fund, and that number has dropped a lot in the last year and a half. The fund's holdings traded at about 39 times earnings at the end of June 2025 and about 35 times earnings on April 30, 2026. By Sept. 30, the number was about 33 times earnings, and on Oct. 31, it was 29.5 times earnings.

    Granted, that last reading came before the latest 10% slide. With earnings held flat, today's price would put the ratio closer to 26 or 27 times earnings.

    That's a massive shift for a share price that is now right back where it was in late April, when it closed around $103. By my rough math, every share of the fund now carries about a third more earnings than it did then.

    In a recent development, the gap to the broader market has shrunk, too. On Oct. 31, the stocks in the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF traded at around 24 times earnings, so the tech fund's premium had fallen to about a quarter. For businesses whose profits are still growing this fast, I think the price is fair.

    It has been revealed that sure, the fund might keep sliding. A correction can become a bear market (a drop of 20% or more), and the fund is already near that mark. And with three stocks making up almost half of its assets, a tough patch for just one of them can drag on the whole fund.

    NYSEMKT · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Industry observers note that but a long holding period changes how much a fall like this matters. After all, this year has already shown how quickly the mood can turn.

    The fund closed at around $84 on March 30 (adjusted for its 8-for-1 stock split in April), and it then rose about 55% to its Oct. 6 high in just over six months.

    No one knows where this sell-off stops. But an investor planning to hold for five or 10 years is largely buying the earnings these companies produce in that stretch. And those earnings seem to have kept climbing through both of this year's sell-offs.

    Industry observers note that is the fund worth buying at around $105 a share? I think so. Its valuation has fallen far more than its price, and its largest companies are still growing. I'd buy the fund now, maybe in a few chunks over the coming months, because the sell-off might go further first.

    It has been revealed that when our analyst team has a stock tip, it can pay to listen. After all, Stock Advisor's total average return is 719%* — a market-crushing outperformance compared to 192% for the S&P 500.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Dividend-paying stocks can enhance portfolio returns by providing a steady income stream to investors and the potential for capital appreciation. Several investors seek exposure to dividend stocks in a volatile backdrop to ensure stable income.

    In this regard, recommendations of top Wall Street analysts can help shortlist attractive dividend stocks, backed by strong financials and cash flows to support consistent dividend payments.

    Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    In a recent development, energy Transfer (ET) is a diversified midstream energy company with about 140,000 miles of pipelines and associated energy infrastructure in 44 states. The company made a quarterly cash distribution of 34 cents per common unit for the second quarter of 2026. At an annualized payment of $1.36 per common unit, ET offers a yield of 6.3%.

    Recently, JPMorgan analyst Jeremy Tonet reiterated a buy rating on Energy Transfer stock and slightly raised his price target to $25 from $24. The analyst noted that the company delivered a strong Q2 beat across all key metrics.

    Recent findings suggest that tonet highlighted that Energy Transfer raised its 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $18.8 billion-$19.1 billion from $18.2 billion-$18.6 billion, reflecting robust base results and cost optimization. The 5-star analyst added that the firm "tightened" its capex to $5.6 billion–$5.9 billion and expects capex above $5 billion annually through 2029, given solid opportunities.

    According to recent reports, about the Hugh Brinson pipeline, Tonet noted Phase 1 (1.5 bcfd) reaching full capacity by September 1 and Phase II capacity (0.7 bcfd) going online by Q1 2027. The analyst also noted completion of a 14-mile Hugh Brinson lateral in Abilene, Texas, and final stages of talks for an additional 250 mmcfd of Oklahoma power plant demand.

    "All in, we see ET well positioned to continue capitalizing on organic growth opportunities across the value chain," remarked Tonet.

    Tonet ranks No. 922 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 57% of the time, delivering an average return of 9%. See Energy Transfer Financials on TipRanks.

    This week's second dividend pick is independent oil and natural gas firm Permian Resources (PR). The company declared a base dividend of $0.16 per share for the third quarter, payable on September 30, 2026. At an annualized dividend of $0.64 per share, PR offers a yield of about 2.7%.

    Recently, Goldman Sachs analyst Neil Mehta reiterated a buy rating on Permian Resources stock and increased his price target to $27 from $22, citing an improved outlook on oil production growth and operational efficiencies.

    According to recent reports, the 5-star analyst noted that while PR stock has outperformed its peers so far in 2026, he sees further upside. Mehta is confident about the tech giant's operational improvements and ability to deliver incremental free cash flow per share through the strategic ground game program. He added that the program has completed about $1.05 billion in bolt-on deals this year (as of August 5).

    "We see the continued success of PR's ground game as constructive toward future inventory replenishment and increasing working interest over time," noted Mehta.

    The analyst also emphasized Permian Resources' solid track record of generating growth in free cash flow (FCF) per share. Mehta expects the firm's free cash flow per share to grow at a 20% CAGR (compound annual growth rate) from 2025–2028.

    Mehta ranks No. 401 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 64% of the time, delivering an average return of 12.8%. See Permian Resources Statistics on TipRanks.

    Moving on to Sempra Energy (SRE), a utility holding manufacturer. Earlier this month, the company declared a quarterly dividend of $0.6575 per share, payable on October 15. At an annualized dividend of $2.63 per share, SRE stock offers a yield of about 3.1%.

    Industry observers note that recently, Jefferies analyst Julien Dumoulin-Smith upgraded SRE stock to Buy from Hold but slightly lowered the price target to $97 from $101. The 5-star analyst noted that Sempra stock is trading at a price/earnings multiple that is 14% below its electric peers due to concerns about Texas transmission capital expenditure and the failure of California legislation.

    Smith noted that the derating of weaker California peers PG&E (PCG) and Edison International (EIX) is weighing on the sum-of-the-parts (SOTP) valuation but is becoming less relevant given their materially higher fire risk compared to Sempra Energy.

    Recent findings suggest that furthermore, Smith expects Sempra Energy's Texas capex initiative to stay in place despite the opposition to transmission and data centers, though delays to 765-kV projects are likely. While a full recovery for SRE stock will need a clearer outcome from the Texas legislative session, Smith believes that the stock may already be an early opportunity for patient investors.

    "We are early on the upgrade but see limited downside at current levels as the market is pricing in little transmission upside," said Smith.

    In a recent development, smith ranks No. 945 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 61% of the time, delivering an average return of 8.2%. See Sempra ETF Exposure on TipRanks.
