    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that tesla (TSLA -7.64%) knows how to get people talking and investors hyped.
    • Recent findings suggest that can Tesla defend its customer base?
    • Industry observers note that none of those questions gets answered by an impressive product demonstration (the Roadster).
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Daniel Miller – Nov 22, 2026 at 9:00PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Tesla ›.

    Recent findings suggest that tesla (TSLA -7.64%) knows how to get people talking and investors hyped. Futuristic vehicles, robotaxis, and humanoid robots give investors plenty to chew on. Those ideas are awesome, but the investment story also depends on less glamorous questions.

    Recent findings suggest that can Tesla defend its customer base? How expensive could its legal battles become? And will its next massive manufacturing bet be as lucrative as investors hope?

    Industry observers note that none of those questions gets answered by an impressive product demonstration (the Roadster). Here are three challenges worth keeping on investors' radar.

    Industry observers note that tesla's domestic sales in China dropped 66.1% year over year to 8,817 vehicles in October. China's battery-electric passenger-car market declined just 5.3%, making it difficult to blame Tesla's entire slide on a struggling market.

    Tesla's Shanghai factory exports provided a cushion, increasing roughly 66% to 59,012 vehicles. Tesla typically emphasizes exports early in a quarter, so October alone should be taken with a grain of salt. Still, its Chinese retail sales have declined year over year for five consecutive months.

    The catch is that competitors are chasing overseas buyers, too, because China's domestic market can't seem to escape a nasty price war. BYD's (BYDDY -4.27%) overseas shipments jumped roughly 103% in October, helping counter sluggish demand and intense price competition at home.

    Recent findings suggest that exports give Tesla another outlet, but they don't give it an escape hatch from competition. The investor question is whether it can defend sales and pricing as rivals expand internationally, because Chinese autos are spreading globally, and rapidly.

    Tesla's technology promises also carry a growing legal exposure. An April Electrek analysis estimated potential financial exposure across lawsuits and regulatory matters at $2.7 billion to $14.5 billion. To be clear, that's an outside estimate of possible outcomes -- not an amount Tesla owes, has reserved, or expects to pay.

    It has been revealed that for something more concrete, consider the Benavides Autopilot case. A jury awarded $129 million in compensatory damages, assigning Tesla 33% of the fault, plus $200 million in punitive damages. Tesla's portion works out to approximately $243 million. The firm is appealing, according to its latest quarterly filing.

    Sources indicate that the legal picture isn't moving entirely against Tesla, either. Its filing also disclosed that an appeals court vacated class certification in a separate driver-assistance advertising case in October. That case returned to the lower court for further proceedings.

    Tesla states it cannot reasonably estimate potential losses in these matters. Investors shouldn't treat the $14.5 billion estimate as an incoming invoice, but unfavorable outcomes could still produce substantial expenses or cash payments.

    If there's one word Wall Street strongly dislikes, it's uncertainty. Legal uncertainty and potential costs deserve a place alongside the excitement about what Tesla's fresh businesses bring to the table.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    According to recent reports, musk claims Tesla will wind down Cybertruck production at its Texas factory around mid-2027 to make room for more Cybercabs. Tesla is choosing where to put valuable manufacturing resources.

    Changing direction can be sensible, especially considering the Cybertruck failed to gain traction with consumers. Sticking with a product just because management once loved it would hardly be a winning strategy.

    Recent findings suggest that on the flip side, building more Cybercabs isn't the same as building a profitable robotaxi business. Tesla needs enough paying rides to cover vehicles, charging, maintenance, insurance, and fleet operations.

    Further, Tesla needs to walk before it can run. There's also a compliance question. In September, federal regulators opened an investigation into Tesla's self-certification that Cybercab meets federal safety standards. To be clear, that inquiry isn't a finding of anything wrong, but it highlights another factor to consider beyond factory production.

    Factory floor space doesn't pay shareholders back on enthusiasm or hype alone. Investors need evidence that the business replacing the Cybertruck can generate attractive returns, and right now we have a lot of hype but also many questions.

    Industry observers note that tesla's ambitions remain compelling, and also a little daunting, if investors are honest about the firm turning from a vehicle manufacturer to more of a technology conglomerate. But defending its customer base at home and abroad, managing legal exposure and regulatory hurdles, and turning robotaxis into a worthwhile business will help determine how much of that promise reaches shareholders.

    In a recent development, enjoy the futuristic vehicles, barrel rolls, and all. Just keep an eye on the business paying to develop that wild future.

    By Jennifer Saibil – Nov 22, 2026 at 10:00PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing ›.

    Despite outstanding results for its latest quarter, Nvidia (NVDA -14.01%) stock keeps sinking. It's down 19% year-to-date, and it's clear that, for the time being, investors are concerned about what's coming up for the artificial intelligence (AI) powerhouse.

    Investors like to avoid uncertainty, although no one ever knows what will happen next; the entire episode was unexpected. However, some companies have tried-and-true businesses that can withstand rigorous investor scrutiny, minimizing their risk.

    If you're looking for a top AI organization that fits the bill, consider Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM -9.48%).

    Investors are worried about Nvidia for several reasons right now. No one knows what Nvidia will look like without Jensen Huang at its helm, and CFO and interim CEO Colette Kress has remarked that deals that resemble "circular financing" will be toned down.

    According to recent reports, the changes in business approach could impact the firm's financials, although Kress assured investors that demand is high, and she raised the fiscal 2028 revenue growth outlook from 70% to 75%. "Our momentum is real. Our demand is accelerating. Our supply is growing." She stated on Nvidia's 2027 third-quarter (ended Oct. 25) earnings call, "Our customers and our partners are with us... We've got this.".

    Image source: Taiwan Semiconductor.

    Sources indicate that many AI companies are feeling market concern, including Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Firm (TSMC). Nvidia is its largest client, overtaking Apple (AAPL -1.90%) in importance, and one of the main beneficiaries of TSMC's expansion to Arizona, its first U.S.-based facility. Kress noted that Nvidia's suppliers and partners are all behind it, and that it has secured the necessary memory and packaging to resume business as normal. She called out Taiwan Semi specifically, saying, "I see right now the leadership even from TSMC that was in our offices just this week, also fully engaged in helping us.".

    TSMC stock is still up 19% year-to-date, outperforming the S&P 500 (^GSPC -3.70%), even though it's 25% off its high.

    While Nvidia and TSMC's success are to some degree tied together, TSMC had an excellent business before Nvidia, and it can maintain a strong business even if Nvidia does slow down. While Nvidia accounts for 22% of TSMC's revenue, it's been demanding capacity that could go to other players. In the third quarter, high-performance computing, which is where AI is, accounted for 68% of total revenue, up 22% from last year.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    According to recent reports, the company's broad diversification is one of the features I always point out, and here is a live example of why that's critical. TSMC is a foundry that works with many partner clients globally. It makes semiconductors for all kinds of industries, which is why it can continue to grow even as tech trends and leaders change. There's no reason to panic about Nvidia's dominant position at this time, but whoever is in the lead will likely work with TSMC.

    Recent findings suggest that the tech giant's fresh Arizona location provides greater capacity and helps it avoid tariffs. It also keeps it closer to its U.S. clients. It still has major expansion intends, including more buildings at the Arizona facility, and it has a location in Washington.

    Sources indicate that nvidia chips drive AI development, since the hyperscalers use its best-in-class chips. The fresh Vera Rubin system, which includes chips and computers, is in high demand. But TSMC plays an key role in making that happen, since it has the capacity to keep the chips coming. CEO C.C. Wei noted that there are several approaches to AI development right now, but since TSMC has "technology leadership, manufacturing excellence, global capacity expansion, and customer trust," all the players partner with it.

    In a recent development, performance has been fantastic, fueled by AI. Sales increased 41% year over year (currency-neutral) in the third quarter, and gross margin improved by 6.9 percentage points. It was lower sequentially due to higher costs and growth investments. Management repeated that "a higher level of capital expenditures is always correlated with higher growth opportunities in the following years.".

    Recent findings suggest that if AI does slow down, Taiwan Semi might, too. It's not a sure thing, but even if it does happen, it isn't likely to last.

    At the current price, TSMC stock trades at a price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 23, which is a fantastic deal on a growth stock that will continue to drive AI development and other technology.

    Comcast vs. Walt Disney: Which Media Stock Is a Better Buy?

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Jack Delaney – Updated Nov 22, 2026 at 10:00PM EST.
    • It has been revealed that is the future of media found in the cables under the street or the stories on the screen?
    • According to recent reports, comcast operates as a backbone of modern connectivity while diversifying into world-class entertainment and theme parks.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Jack Delaney – Updated Nov 22, 2026 at 10:00PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Comcast ›.

    It has been revealed that is the future of media found in the cables under the street or the stories on the screen? Investors often choose between Comcast (CMCSA +0.16%) and Walt Disney (DIS -1.89%) for diversified exposure.

    According to recent reports, comcast operates as a backbone of modern connectivity while diversifying into world-class entertainment and theme parks. Disney remains the gold standard for intellectual property, using its content library to fuel a massive ecosystem of streaming and travel. Comparing them helps clarify whether you prefer reliable utility-like cash flow or brand-driven growth.

    Comcast provides broadband, wireless, and video services to millions of customers, largely under its Xfinity and Comcast Business brands. As one of the prominent media stocks, it also owns NBCUniversal, which produces television and film content and operates Universal theme parks. The manufacturer maintains critical partnerships with providers like Verizon and T-Mobile to support its expanding mobile phone service segment.

    It has been revealed that in the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached nearly $123 billion, which represents a slight decrease of approximately 0.2% compared to the prior year. Net income for this period was roughly $11.3 billion.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Walt Disney focuses on its entertainment, sports, and experiences segments to drive global engagement. The manufacturer leverages iconic franchises through Disney+ and Hulu while managing a massive portfolio of theme parks and cruise lines. It also holds strategic stakes in other platforms, including a 70% interest in FuboTV (FUBO -11.94%) and a 37% interest in JioStar in India.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Comcast faces heavy competition from wireline and wireless broadband providers like Charter Communications (CHTR -3.34%). The continued rise of streaming services threatens the profitability of its linear network agreements and traditional video packages. Furthermore, technological shifts such as generative artificial intelligence and a $117.5 million data breach settlement represent significant operational hurdles.

    According to recent reports, walt Disney has an intense rivalry for viewers and advertising dollars and competes with tech giants like Amazon (AMZN -4.10%) and Apple (AAPL -1.90%). Operational risks include the potential for labor strikes among park employees or entertainment guilds, as well as service blackouts during contract negotiations. Additionally, the company must manage the volatility of consumer spending on high-end vacations and cruise ship voyages.

    Comcast trades at a significant discount based on its forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio, which compares the stock price to future earnings estimates, and its price-to-sales (P/S) ratio, which measures market value against sales over the past twelve months.

    In a recent development, deciding between Disney and Comcast really comes down to what you're looking to accomplish with your portfolio, as well as your risk tolerance. That said, between the two, I would lean toward owning Comcast over Disney.

    Industry observers note that one of the main reasons is that investors seem to be taking on less expectation risk with Comcast than with Disney. In the third quarter of 2026, Comcast generated $4.2 billion in free cash flow, giving it significant flexibility amid considerable uncertainty in the markets and the economy. While still impressive, Disney's free cash flow of $3 billion in its third quarter is noticeably less.

    For Comcast, its broadband business has some challenges, but its wireless segment is growing promptly and could offset weakness in that division if it continues to expand.

    In a recent development, disney may be a more exciting investment and has more stock price growth potential. Still, in this kind of market, I'd rather own the stock that generates more free cash flow and passes it on to its shareholders through a dividend that yields 5.3%.

Let's look at five growth stocks that have the potential to double by 2028 and what would need to happen for them to achieve that.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Despite its size, SpaceX (SPCX -7.69%) has clear potential to double in the next two years. For this to happen, it's going to have to grow rapidly and continue to hit important technological milestones, like it did when it recently caught the upper stage of its Starship rocket.

    In a recent development, much of SpaceX's growth in the next two years will come from its infrastructure-as-a-service business. To rapidly grow this business, it's going to add a lot of compute capacity while maintaining its strong payback periods. If it can navigate permitting issues and industry bottlenecks and hit its growth targets of adding 10 gigawatts of power next year, and do that again in 2028, the stock could double.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Industry observers note that the market is shifting toward custom artificial intelligence (AI) chips and inference, which plays right into Broadcom's (AVGO -12.19%) wheelhouse. With the stock trading at a forward price-to-earnings (P/E) multiple of just 11 times fiscal 2028 analyst estimates (ending October 2028), it has a substantial opportunity to double in the next two years.

    For this to happen, the manufacturer is going to have to maintain solid hardware gross margins and not lose significant share in the application-specific integrated circuit (ASIC) market to cheaper competitors in future chip iterations. It's also going to have to see large customers Anthropic (ANT -8.50%) and OpenAI thrive, as much of its future projected custom chip revenue is coming from these two customers and Alphabet (GOOGL -2.70%) (GOOG -2.59%).

    Trading at a huge discount to larger cybersecurity rivals while growing promptly, SentinelOne (S -4.58%) stock could easily double from continued growth and multiple expansion.     The firm has been aggressively making moves to become a strong provider in the AI era, and if this leads to accelerating growth, the stock has a great opportunity to double. Analysts at Wedbush, meanwhile, noted after talking to vendors and resellers that customers were starting to expand with SentinelOne solutions, and the company was winning in the small and medium-sized business (SMB) and mid-market spaces due to its strong abilities and cheaper pricing.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Beaten to a pulp over the past two years, SoundHound AI (SOUN -10.31%) has the potential to see its stock double in the coming years, with its valuation down to a forward P/S multiple under 6. For this to happen, it will need to stabilize and integrate its recent LivePerson acquisition, hit its target of becoming earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) profitable in the second half of 2027, and see strong adoption of OASYS, its fresh voice, language intelligence, and agentic AI orchestration solution.

    In a recent development, the ingredients are all there; it will just be a matter of execution. Right now, the market is betting SoundHound won't be able to pull this off, but if it does, the upside is enormous.

    Industry observers note that stepping outside of the tech sector, Dutch Bros (BROS -4.01%) has one of the best opportunities in the consumer space for its stock to double over the next two years. The coffee shop operator has been delivering strong same-store sales growth while it has huge expansion opportunities. However, the stock has been beaten down over the past year, leaving it at a very attractive P/S valuation compared to rival Starbucks (SBUX -1.28%) despite its much longer growth runway.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • September ended on a mixed note, with the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average falling 0.5% and 4.3%, respectively, while the Nasdaq Composite climbed 1.9%.
    • In this climate, investors with a long-term horizon can track recommendations from top Wall Street analysts to find stocks with solid growth prospects.
    • Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    September ended on a mixed note, with the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average falling 0.5% and 4.3%, respectively, while the Nasdaq Composite climbed 1.9%. Markets remained on edge with higher oil prices and Treasury yields weighing on investor sentiment and triggering fears of additional interest rate hikes.

    In this climate, investors with a long-term horizon can track recommendations from top Wall Street analysts to find stocks with solid growth prospects.

    Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    Neocloud firm CoreWeave (CRWV) is benefiting from robust AI-driven demand for cloud computing.

    In a recent development, recently, JPMorgan analyst Samik Chatterjee upgraded CoreWeave to buy from hold, raising his price target to $125 from $120. The analyst cited favorable pricing, driven by solid demand, for the upgrade.

    Chatterjee remarked CoreWeave is now more willing to sign premium priced, shorter-term contracts, which lift his revenue and margin estimates. CRWV stock performance has been underwhelming as investors worry about high capital spending, the analyst noted. That said, he believes that higher prices and increased margins will more than offset the rise in debt to fund capital spending, improving the stock's valuation.

    Chatterjee noted the 25% price hike in July across CoreWeave's product offerings and frequent price increases by rivals like Nebius (NBIS), adding that some peers are charging nearly three times more for short-term compute contracts than what CoreWeave charges on longer-term deals.

    Recent findings suggest that "CoreWeave's leverage of the opportunity [is] evident in its recent press release highlighting contracts signed in F3Q at ~$40M/MW," stated Chatterjee. JPMorgan said higher pricing is already contributing 5-10 percentage points to contract margins versus earlier deals.

    Sources indicate that chatterjee ranks No. 4 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 75% of the time, delivering an average return of 55.3%. See CoreWeave Statistics on TipRanks.

    Palo Alto Networks (PANW) is a provider of cybersecurity solutions across network, cloud, security operations, AI and identity. Following a discussion with management, BTIG analyst Gray Powell reiterated a buy rating on PANW and raised his price target to $425 from $404.

    After a review of Palo Alto's product-level growth catalysts, Powell sees clear upside to both revenue and next-generation security (NGS) annual recurring revenue (ARR) in fiscal 2027. He expects PANW to deliver pro forma revenue growth of more than 17%, above the consensus estimate of 14.6%, and NGS ARR growth of more than 26% versus the Street's expectation of 24.5%.

    Over the past five years, the Palo Alto business mix, has moved to higher-growth product areas and new markets. from what was earlier viewed as a hardware-centric network security tech giant, Powell noted. The 5-star analyst estimates that hardware firewalls and attached subscriptions now account for less than 50% of revenue.

    Meanwhile, high-growth solutions, including Prisma SASE, software firewalls, Cortex XSIAM, Chronosphere and Idira now represent more than 35% of PANW's revenue. "Investors may not fully realize the growth potential within PANW's platform story," Powell said.

    BTIG is optimistic about the prospects of Chronosphere in observability, CyberArk in identity and software firewalls and Prisma AIRS in the network and AI security business.

    It has been revealed that powell ranks No. 320 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 61% of the time, delivering an average return of 17.3%. See Palo Alto Networks KPIs on TipRanks.

    It has been revealed that in a research note on September 30, Rosenblatt analyst Scott Devitt reiterated a buy rating on e-commerce and cloud computing platform Amazon (AMZN), raising his price target to $360 from $335. Fears that agentic commerce poses a major threat to Amazon's advertising business seem "overstated," he mentioned.

    It has been revealed that devitt noted that the growing adoption of personal agents and AI shopping assistants has sparked concern about displacement of Amazon's retail media business. But the 5-star analyst remains bullish, given Amazon's ability to adapt to changing consumer behavior, as it's done in the past.

    It has been revealed that additionally, Devitt argues that even if an AI agent helps a shopper discover a product, Amazon can still handle the purchase and delivery, keeping much of the transaction value. He highlighted that management believes that existing Amazon shoppers will likely continue to start their shopping journey on the platform because it has better personalization, accurate pricing and inventory information that third-party agents still lack.

    Industry observers note that overall, Devitt expects Amazon's retail business to prove a net beneficiary of agentic commerce. Fewer clicks would not hurt the tech giant if the value of each remaining click and overall volumes keep rising, he remarked. The argument is that even if Amazon loses some sponsored ad revenue over the next few years, it would likely be only a small part of the company's total business and could be offset by growth in other areas.

    "Consistent with our AI framework, we continue to view Amazon as one of the most resilient leaders in our coverage, combining owned compute infrastructure with a physical fulfillment moat," noted Devitt. His bullish view is supported, Devitt said, by expectations that Amazon Web Services (AWS) will exit the year at a more than 45% growth rate with continued margin improvement.

    Devitt ranks No. 765 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 49% of the time, delivering an average return of 12%. See Amazon Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

    #130853. Junk bonds are 'flashing yellow.' Watch these warning signs

    📅 09 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1017 w)
    📖 Baca
    Gadgets ⚠️ Warning 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Junk bonds are 'flashing yellow.' Watch these warning signs

    📅 09 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1017 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Cracks are forming in the junk bond market as investors demand higher payouts for owning the market's riskiest debt.
    • High-yield bonds now yield 8.1%, up from 7.22% a month ago.
    • Sources indicate that the high-yield market is also showing stress on the credit side with spreads recently widening to levels not seen since April, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of St.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Cracks are forming in the junk bond market as investors demand higher payouts for owning the market's riskiest debt. It isn't time to ditch high-yield bonds, but investors should pay attention to the warning signs.

    High-yield bonds now yield 8.1%, up from 7.22% a month ago. The increase reflects a jump in yields across the curve as investors bake in more inflation from high energy prices and other pressures, including concern about the deficit — hitting nearly $2 trillion in the fiscal year that ended Sept. 30.

    Sources indicate that the high-yield market is also showing stress on the credit side with spreads recently widening to levels not seen since April, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis. Credit spreads are the difference in yield between the bonds and Treasurys of similar maturities. Wider spreads mean investors are demanding higher yields for holding corporate debt, viewing it as riskier.

    According to recent reports, spreads are at 315 basis points in the overall high-yield market, higher than a year ago but still below levels in March when they reached 346 bps. One basis point equals one one-hundredth of a percent, or 0.01%.

    Recent findings suggest that the high-yield market consists of bonds rated BB+ by S&P and Fitch and Ba1 and under by Moody's. The lowest-rated cohort, CCC and below, has seen the most movement with spreads climbing dramatically over the past year to roughly 1,250 bps.

    Right now, the high-yield market is "flashing yellow" but is "far from red," remarked Michael Arone, chief investment strategist at State Street Investment Management.

    It makes sense that investors are demanding more compensation for taking on additional credit risk as borrowing costs rise, he stated.

    Yields are elevated across the board with the 10-year Treasury reaching its highest level since 2002 earlier in the week.

    "The bigger question is whether this is simply a repricing of interest rate risk, or the beginning of a more fundamental reassessment of credit quality," Arone said.

    He's in a wait-and-see mode since earnings are still growing, interest-coverage ratios remain good, and while default rates have ticked up some, he believes it is not concerning.

    That stated, the starting point in spreads is likely weighing on investors' psyche, since they are still low by historical standards.

    In a recent development, "There's a small margin of error here, which I also think raises the anxiety level," Arone explained. "The compensation that investors are receiving for taking on this credit risk isn't overwhelming relative to history, and therefore subtle changes in credit spreads can be concerning.".

    While there may be concerns about part of the lower-rated market, the overall high-yield market is in good fundamental shape.

    In fact, credit quality is at a record high, with BB bonds making up over 60% of the market compared with 38% prior to the global financial crisis, said Kelley Gerrity, a fixed income strategist at Morgan Stanley Investment Management.

    "We've had higher-quality companies coming in, and with higher rates now, you also have more discipline from companies that are more indebted ... just because of the higher cost of capital, so that actually is creating a bit of a healthier picture as well," she mentioned.

    The lowest tier of high yield has always been more speculative, since the bonds have a higher default risk. Therefore, it's no surprise that they are the ones seeing the most widening in spreads, noted Collin Martin, head of fixed income research and strategy at the Schwab Center for Financial Research.

    The overall move in high-yield spreads have been "orderly," he noted. "Are there cracks forming? I think the cracks are logical cracks with the lowest-rated bonds and it's too early to say that it's spreading to the broad credit market.".

    It has been revealed that in addition, fluctuations within the CCC-rated and lower spreads have been idiosyncratic, Gerrity added. Morgan Stanley recently broke down the spreads in the lowest cohort into two buckets: performing assets and non-performing assets, which are defined as spreads above 1,000 bps.

    The non-performing spread to worst is 2,818 bps, while the performing bucket — the biggest piece of the CCC market — is 461 bps, she said.

    "It is isolated," she said. "I'm not necessarily sure that that will go away anytime soon, but it doesn't tell the story of overall concern and flashing caution for credit markets right now.".

    For now, investors should remain selective within higher yield, Gerrity advised.

    "We're looking for the best relative value opportunities, and we think that exists within that single-B cohort, and so we're leaning into that," she noted.

    Investors should be concerned if there is a steep widening in the broader high-yield market.

    But there's scant evidence of stress in the BB cohort. Spreads in that group are at 194 bps, up from 179 bps a year ago — although the move hasn't been in a straight line.

    "We're going to be focusing our attention on what are considered some stronger businesses," Martin stated. "If we start to see the markets demand higher spreads there also, that's what we'll be looking at to see if risks are really rising.".

    It's also important to understand that the Federal Reserve is raising rates in a strong economic environment, mentioned R.J. Gallo, chief investment officer of global fixed income at Federated Hermes. The central bank is concerned about an inflation problem amid high fossil fuel prices due to the Iran war, while growth has been stronger than expected, he noted.

    "With growth being good as the reason that the Fed is hiking, then you wouldn't expect high yield to blow out because growth means revenues stay up, means cash flow and profitability stays up," he explained.

    High yield becomes a disaster when the economy is heading into a sharp economic downturn, Gallo said.

    "That's when spreads really widen out," he said. "But a recession is not the odds-on bet. Now, talk to me in six months if the Fed keeps hiking over and over, if oil prices stay high for longer, well, then maybe we will start to wonder.".
